speaker: TONY
line: Sue! SUE!

speaker: LAD
line: You’re alright, you’re alright. I’ve got you.

speaker: LAD
line: Is your dad alright? He looked like he was going to go over.

speaker: SUE
line: He’s fine. Thanks, love.

speaker: TONY
line: She didn’t correct him. I’m her husband. And I couldn’t get ten feet to my own wife.

speaker: SUE
line: He has no idea what I saw from behind that van.

speaker: SUE
line: Are we going to talk about it?

speaker: TONY
line: What do you want me to say?

speaker: SUE
line: I want you to say you’re going to do something. Because if that lad hadn’t been there, Tony…

speaker: TONY
line: I’d have got to you.

speaker: SUE
line: You didn’t make it one step.

speaker: SUE
line: I’m 52. I’m not ready to push you round in a chair.

speaker: TONY
line: Nobody’s pushing me anywhere.

speaker: SUE
line: Then why did he think you were my dad?

speaker: TONY
line: I’ll sort it. I’m not living like this.

speaker: TONY
line: Sixty-four. Thirty years laying patios. I’ve knelt on every drive in this street. Now I can’t get across a car park to my own wife.

place: rock bottom — his stairs sideways, the drawer, waiting in the car
speaker: TONY
line: I used to carry her bags in from the car. Now I wait in the car while she loads the boot.

speaker: GP
line: Your bloods are fine. Blood pressure’s fine. For 64 you’re in decent nick.

speaker: TONY
line: I’m 64 and I walk like I’m 85.

speaker: GP
line: Thirty years on your knees, Tony. It’s wear and tear. It’s very normal.

speaker: TONY
line: It’s not normal.

speaker: GP
line: Keep moving, lose a few pounds, paracetamol when it’s bad. That works for most people.

speaker: TONY
line: Gary. I’ve got to ask. How? You’re six years older than me.

speaker: GARY
line: You want the real answer?

speaker: TONY
line: I’ve done the physio. The tablets. I’ve got a drawer full of braces. Nothing shifts it.

speaker: GARY
line: It won’t. Two years ago I was worse than you. I went down my stairs on my backside.

speaker: TONY
line: Give over.

speaker: GARY
line: I’m serious. And I’d tried everything you’re trying now.

speaker: TONY
line: So what changed?

speaker: GARY
line: Let me ask you something first. Where does it hurt? All round the knee, or one spot?

speaker: TONY
line: All round. I don’t know.

speaker: GARY
line: Press there. Just under the kneecap. Two fingers down.

speaker: TONY
line: There.

speaker: GARY
line: Exactly. That’s what nobody tells us. Every bloke our age thinks his knee’s worn out. So we rest it, strap it, take the tablets, and blame our age when nothing changes.

speaker: GARY
line: But that’s not your knee giving up. It’s that one spot. Every step down the stairs, seventeen times your bodyweight goes through it. A spot the size of a coin. The pain is pressure. Nothing more.

speaker: TONY
line: So how do you fix it?

speaker: GARY
line: You can’t rest it off. A brace goes round the joint. A sleeve squeezes it. A tablet hides it. None of them take the weight off that spot.

speaker: GARY
line: You’re not old, Tony. You’re overloaded. That’s why nothing’s worked. You’ve been fighting a pressure problem with paracetamol.

speaker: TONY
line: So what did you do?

speaker: GARY
line: I took the weight off it. Stryde. It’s a strap. Sits right on that spot, two centimetres under the kneecap. Catches the force before it hits the knee. Three years they spent on it with orthopaedic surgeons.

speaker: GARY
line: Don’t buy the cheap ones off Amazon. They stretch. Anything that stretches doesn’t work.

speaker: TONY
line: A strap? Come off it.

speaker: GARY
line: I know. I said the same. Laughed at my wife when she ordered it. And that’s it. That’s what changed. Put it on and go down your own stairs. You’ll know in a minute.

speaker: SUE
line: What’s that?

speaker: TONY
line: Something Gary put me on.

speaker: SUE
line: You’ve said that before.

speaker: TONY
line: Then don’t watch.
